A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe Object-WIPER and include the same six-page supplementary material. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the scientific content is unchanged and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on DAVIS and WIPER-Bench, component and masking ablations, a human preference study, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, human preference study, and runtime measurements, including the supplementary results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical associated-effect localization, inversion, adaptive masking, attention scaling, reinitialization, and background-value copying procedures. No model component or algorithm changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate on DAVIS and the same 60-video WIPER-Bench. The associated-effect categories and complex scenarios described in Sections 5 and 8 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark, localization, and runtime comparisons. In Table 2, Gen-Prop remains evaluated only on DAVIS, with no WIPER-Bench results.

E3.justification: The preprocessing, model configurations, evaluation metrics, human-study design, and runtime protocol remain identical in the main text and supplement. No experimental settings are revised.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3 and Figure 8, text-token and localization analyses in Section 12, and masking ablations in Table 5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 13 retains runtime averaging over 10 runs, and Section 11.2 retains the same inter-rater reliability analysis using Fleiss' kappa. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practices change.

E6.justification: All quantitative entries and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains Object-WIPER TokSim scores of 32.80 on DAVIS and 33.09 on WIPER-Bench; supplementary human-study and runtime results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for attention, masking, and TokSim, including Equations 1–8 and the notation table, are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: training-free object and effect removal, adaptive masking, TokSim, WIPER-Bench, and superiority over evaluated baselines on TokSim.

C2.justification: The interpretations of component contributions and metric behavior are unchanged. Section 10 retains the same limitations concerning inversion reconstruction, background preservation, and the underlying video model's capacity.

D1.justification: Dataset construction, implementation details, hyperparameters, and resource-access statements are unchanged. The new acknowledgment credits annotation and baseline assistance without adding technical procedures or reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: All 48 references and the related-work positioning remain unchanged. The acknowledgment of discussions about GenProp introduces neither a new cited work nor a revised relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short acknowledgments paragraph before the references, crediting discussions, dataset annotation, and baseline assistance. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added acknowledgments shift the bibliography across columns and pages 9–10. All figures, tables, captions, and supplementary layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds contributor credit but leaves the methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations unchanged throughout the paper and supplement. The acknowledgment and resulting bibliography reflow do not materially improve or diminish overall paper quality.
